item.title: Gold Miner Cadillac, Backers Raise C$385 Million in Canada IPO
item.description: Cadillac Mines Corp. and some of its backers raised C$385 million ($273 million) in an upsized initial public offering, adding to the mining-driven rebound of listing activity in Canada.

item.title: Trump Tariffs: How US Is Maintaining Import Duties Using Section 301
item.description: From the start of his second term, US President Donald Trump made clear he would put tariffs at the center of US economic policy. When the Supreme Court invalidated sweeping import duties he’d imposed citing emergency powers, he used a different provision — Section 122 of the Trade Act of 1974, to set a flat 10% levy on imports. Such tariffs are time-limited, however, and Trump’s expired on July 24.

item.title: BlackRock Kicks Off $12.3 Billion Bond Sale for Meta Data Center
item.description: BlackRock Inc. began marketing $12.3 billion of high-grade bonds to fund a Meta Platforms Inc. data center project, testing investor appetite amid growing concerns about excessive AI infrastructure spending.

item.title: Gilts Caught Between Twin Risks From Burnham Debut and Oil Shock
item.description: Britain’s bond traders have spent Andy Burnham’s first week in office trying to price two different forces: the spending ambitions of his new government and the impact of oil prices hovering near $100 a barrel.

item.title: S&P 500 Futures Steady as Big Tech Rebounds, Oil Dips Below $100
item.description: US equity futures on Friday were little changed, indicating stocks are poised to steady from the deepest one-day drop in a month, as Brent crude prices fell below $100 a barrel and a selloff in Big Tech shares eased.

item.title: Profits Are Beating a High Bar and Traders Still Aren’t Enthused
item.description: Corporate earnings strong enough to beat the highest expectations in years have failed to impress investors fretting about AI spending and economic growth.

item.title: Momentum Crash Hits YOLO Traders’ Returns by Most in Four Years
item.description: A rapid selloff in the high-flying momentum trade is wrecking the strategy’s staunchest bulls: Retail traders.

item.title: CATL First-Half Profit Jumps 42% on Energy Storage Tailwind
item.description: Contemporary Amperex Technology Co. Ltd. posted a 42% increase in first-half profit as the world’s largest electric-vehicle battery maker benefited from robust demand for energy-storage systems.

item.description: Spiking energy prices, more US tariffs and mushrooming spending on artificial intelligence are reawakening investors’ inflation fears.

item.title: Mauritius Eyes $50 Billion GDP to Reach High-Income Status
item.description: Mauritius seeks to more than triple gross domestic product to $50 billion by 2050 to achieve its goal of becoming a high-income industrialized economy driven by sectors including pharmaceuticals, finance and tourism.

item.title: Dangote Targets $100 Billion Empire With Oil and Fertilizers
item.description: Aliko Dangote is betting that Africa’s largest refinery, the continent’s biggest cement producer and his fertilizer businesses will expand his empire fivefold to $100 billion by the end of the decade.

item.title: Travelers Draws Wave of Bears as Stock Eyes Best Year Since 2000
item.description: The best year for Travelers Companies Inc. shares in more than 25 years has unleashed a bevy of downgrades as Wall Street bets that the stock’s gains have peaked.

item.title: Verizon Beats on Wireless, Internet Revenue Amid Turnaround
item.description: Verizon Communications Inc. reported mobility and broadband sales that exceeded Wall Street’s expectations in the second quarter, signaling that Chief Executive Officer Dan Schulman’s turnaround plan is starting to bear fruit.

item.title: ‘Ridiculously Tight’ US Preferred Spreads Risk Trapping Buyers
item.description: US banks are raising regulatory capital at the tightest valuations since the financial crisis, unsettling the most seasoned investors.

item.title: Samsung, SK Hynix to Ink Large Chip Supply Deals With US Firms
item.description: Samsung Electronics Co. and SK Hynix Inc. are set to unveil major agreements involving “very large” sums with leading US technology companies during President Lee Jae Myung’s visit to Silicon Valley, a senior presidential official said.

item.title: Russia Cuts Key Rate to 14% as Drone Strikes Batter Economy
item.description: Russia’s central bank extended its yearlong monetary easing cycle, delivering a token reduction in borrowing costs and providing a small measure of relief to businesses facing their bleakest conditions since the war on Ukraine began.

item.title: Moneta Bank CEO Sees Chance Czech Rates Will Rise Further
item.description: Czech interest rates are likely to remain elevated for the “foreseeable future,” with the odds pointing to a further hike in borrowing costs, Moneta Money Bank Chief Executive Officer Tomas Spurny said.

item.title: Dollar Set for Best Week in a Month as Haven Flows Offer Support
item.description: The dollar is heading for its best week in a month as investors return to the traditional haven amid heightened geopolitical tensions.

item.title: Gulf States Set for Debt Binge to Build Routes Avoiding Hormuz
item.description: Traders are preparing for a spike in borrowing from Persian Gulf nations as the region’s oil exporters seek financing to build costly bypasses around the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: ECB Still More Likely to Hike Rates Than Hold, Simkus Says
item.description: The European Central Bank is still more likely to increase borrowing costs than to hold them steady, according Governing Council member Gediminas Simkus.

item.title: EU Escalates TikTok Probe Over Lack of Teen Privacy Protections
item.description: The European Union escalated a probe against TikTok under its content moderation rulebook, accusing the social network of failing to protect the safety and privacy of teen users.

item.title: Economists Stick to Fed Rate Cut Call as Markets Price In Hikes
item.description: Economists continue to expect the Federal Reserve’s next move will be an interest-rate cut even as financial markets price in higher borrowing costs by the end of the year.

item.title: Euronext Mulls Setting Up a Private Market to Rival the UK’s
item.description: Euronext NV is considering creating a market for private securities, potentially ramping up competition with the London Stock Exchange Group Plc as bourses seek to offer investors access to fast-growing private companies.

item.title: BofA’s Raedler Says Investors Are Ignoring Stock-Market Risks
item.description: Stock markets are pricing in a scenario where everything goes right, leaving investors uncompensated for mounting risks, according to Sebastian Raedler, head of European equity strategy at Bank of America Corp.

item.title: UK Food Prices to Peak Lower Than Thought, BOE Survey Finds
item.description: Britain’s supermarkets plan to raise food prices by less than previously thought as rising fuel costs caused by the Middle East conflict dents household demand, the Bank of England’s survey of regional business contacts said.
